hints: What do the three corner angles of any triangle always add up to?
If two corners were both 90 degrees, how much would be left over for the third corner?

canonical: The three corner angles of a triangle always add up to 180 degrees.
Two square (90-degree) corners alone would already add up to 180 degrees, leaving nothing for the third corner — so a triangle can have at most 1 square corner.

stem: A triangle has 3 straight sides and 3 corners, and its corner angles always add up to 180 degrees in total. What is the greatest number of square (90-degree) corners it can have at the same time?
